prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The algorithm is **Timsort**—a stable, adaptive comparison sort with **O(n)** best-case and **O(n log n)** worst-case time.

Strictly speaking, standard Timsort uses **O(n)** auxiliary space, so it is not in-place under the strict O(1)-extra-space definition. If “in-place” is essential, an algorithm such as **WikiSort** is a better match.
